hld-scalability-basics.title: Scalability Foundations
hld-scalability-basics.intro: The opening framework of every system design interview: bottlenecks, horizontal scaling, statelessness, and capacity thinking.
groups: Principles Before Diagrams

• Requirements first: functional (what features) vs non-functional (scale numbers, latency targets, consistency budget, availability %) — senior candidates EXTRACT these aloud before drawing.
• Scale vocabulary: users → QPS (avg vs peak, read:write ratio) → data size → working set. Every design decision traces back to one of these four.
• Bottleneck ladder as systems grow: app CPU → DB connections/IO → network fan-out → coordination costs. Identify the CURRENT bottleneck before optimizing imaginary ones.
• Vertical-first honesty: single beefy box + replicas handles astonishing scale (Stack Overflow ran on ~2 SQL servers for years!) — distributed complexity must be EARNED.
• Availability math: 99.9% = 8.7h down/year; 99.99% = 52min — nines cost nonlinearly; ask what SLA the product actually needs.
Stateless Application Tier

• Golden rule: any server can serve any request → no sticky sessions required → horizontal scaling trivial → deploys/failures invisible.
• Where state goes instead: sessions in Redis (with TTL), files in object storage (S3), user state in DB/cache — the refactor story of 'make it stateless' is a common follow-up.
• Config via environment/feature-flags not local files; immutable deployments (bake AMIs/containers) beat snowflake mutation.
• Graceful shutdown: stop accepting → drain in-flight (LB deregisters first!) → exit; rolling deploys with readiness probes gate traffic.
• Autoscaling signals: CPU is laggy proxy; prefer request-rate/queue-depth/custom metrics; scale-out cooldowns prevent flapping.
Read Path Scaling

• Read:write ratios drive everything — social feeds 100:1+ favor caching/read replicas; write-heavy metrics favor queues/batching.
• Replicas for read scale + HA; replication lag = staleness budget; route read-your-writes via token-based pinning (store LSN after write).
• Cache layers stacked: browser → CDN → app-local LRU → shared Redis → origin; each layer's hit ratio compounds offload.
• Denormalization as read-path weapon: precomputed counters/join tables updated async; consistency traded consciously per field.
• Numbers drill: 10k QPS reads × 2KB responses = 20MB/s egress trivially CDN-able; same QPS hitting Postgres needs pool math + replica fanout — quantify before choosing.
Write Path Scaling

• Batch everything possible: group commits, bulk inserts, log aggregation — syscall/network amortization multiplies throughput.
• Queue between spikes and storage: absorb bursts, smooth to steady ingest rate; consumers scale independently (Kafka partition parallelism).
• Sharding when vertical exhausted: pick key by access pattern (user-id for social, tenant-id B2B); Instagram's logical-shard trick pre-decouples.
• Write contention killers: hot-row updates (counters) → shard counters + periodic merge; last-block inserts (monotonic index tails) → ordered-but-distributed IDs (snowflake).
• Async-by-default posture: anything not needing synchronous response (emails, analytics, thumbnails) leaves the critical path immediately.
Capacity Estimation Habits

• Back-of-envelope reflexes: traffic (QPS peak = 3× avg), storage (row_size × rows × years × replication × overhead), bandwidth (QPS × response size), memory (hot set ≤ RAM×0.7).
• Standard figures memorized: char=1B(ASCII)/2-4B(UTF-8), int=4B, UUID=16B(raw)/36B(text), timestamp=8B, typical tweet ~300B, photo ~200KB-1MB.
• Power-of-two fluency: 1M req/day ≈ 12/s; 100M ≈ 1.2k/s; 1B ≈ 12k/s — instant conversions during interviews.
• Growth headroom: design for 2-3× current load, not 100× (YAGNI applies to infra too — saying so reads mature).
• Cost sanity: rough $ per GB-month (S3 ~0.023, NVMe instance higher), egress $/GB shaping multi-region choices — dollar-aware designs impress.
Scaling Journey Narrative

• Stage 1: monolith + managed DB + CDN (most companies should STOP here longer than they do).
• Stage 2: read replicas + Redis + stateless autoscale — buys enormous headroom cheaply.
• Stage 3: queue-offloaded async workloads + targeted denormalization + maybe read-heavy service splits.
• Stage 4: sharding/partitioning specific hot datasets, cell-based architecture for blast-radius control (Slack's cells story good citation).
• Interview framing: narrate YOUR design through these stages triggered by explicit triggers ('when writes exceed X...') — shows judgment sequencing rather than resume-driven architecture.

hld-load-balancing.title: Load Balancing
hld-load-balancing.intro: L4 vs L7, algorithm zoo, health checking, global steering — plus the failure modes that make LBs interesting.
groups: Why & Where Load Balancers Sit

• Purposes: distribute load, hide failures (health-checked failover), scale horizontally transparently, TLS termination, zero-downtime deploys via drain.
• Positions: DNS (coarse) → GSLB/global → edge/anycast ingress → L4 tier → L7 tier → service-mesh sidecars east-west — each hop solves a different granularity problem.
• Hardware lineage (F5/Citrix) → software era (nginx/haproxy/envoy) → cloud LBs (ALB/NLB/GLB) — knowing tradeoffs of self-hosted-vs-managed scores ops maturity.
• Direct Server Return modes bypass return path for high-throughput L4 (DSR), asymmetric flows with conntrack sync for stateful failover — deep-cut differentiators.
• Client-side balancing alternative: fat-client libraries with endpoint lists (gRPC name resolution, Netflix Ribbon legacy) — push complexity to clients tradeoff.
L4 vs L7 Tradeoffs

• L4 (TCP/UDP): sees only addr/port — blazing fast, protocol-agnostic, can't route by URL/header; connection symmetry issues with DSR.
• L7 (HTTP): parses requests → content routing (/api vs /static), sticky sessions via cookies, compression, WAF integration; costs more CPU per conn, HOL at HTTP layer if mishandled.
• Modern stack pattern: NLB-style L4 fronting ALB-style L7 fleet fronting app pods — layered defense each doing what it's best at.
• TLS termination placement: L4 passthrough preserves end-to-end certs (mTLS chains intact) vs L7 termination enables header manipulation + caching — security/compliance decides.
• HTTP/2&3 wrinkles: h2 multiplexes over ONE conn → least_conn useless (all conns equal!); QUIC connection migration breaks 5-tuple affinity — LBs need protocol awareness (envoy h3 support narrative).
Algorithm Zoo

• Round robin: naive but fine homogeneous pools. Weighted RR for heterogeneity. Least connections: adapts to request-cost variance — default recommendation most times.
• Least response time / resource-based (reports from agents): adaptive flavors; consistency vs freshness of stats tradeoff.
• Random + power-of-two-choices: pick two random backends, take less-loaded — near-optimal with O(1) state (great theory flex, Mitzenmacher result).
• Consistent hashing: ring/ketama or maglev table — request-affinity for caches/uploads survives membership churn; superset/magnet strategies minimize disruption (Google paper worth citing).
• Session stickiness menu: source-IP (breaks behind corporate NATs), cookie insertion/app-controlled — prefer app-level identity stickiness where correctness demands it.
Health Checking & Failure Handling

• Active checks: synthetic probes at interval — too-aggressive DDoSes backends, too-slow detection delays removal; tune thresholds×window.
• Passive checks: observe REAL request outcomes — catches gray failures active probes miss (disk full only breaking some paths).
• Outlier ejection (envoy model): consecutive 5xx → eject for base-ejection-time × multipliers; panic mode when >50% unhealthy → fail-open rather than total outage — nuanced behavior worth naming.
• Slow-start ramp for newly-added backends (JIT-compiled services warmup); circuit-breaker integration at client side complements LB ejection.
• Gray-failure philosophy: the hardest failures are partial (one AZ's replication slow) — observability feeding adaptive routing is frontier practice (read the Azure gray-failure paper!).
Global Traffic Steering

• DNS-GSLB: geo/latency-weighted answers, health-checked failover at DNS TTL speed (minutes worst case) — coarse but global.
• Anycast: same IP announced everywhere, BGP proximity wins naturally; failure = withdraw prefix (convergence seconds-minutes); combine with per-PoP internal LBs — Cloudflare/Fastly model.
• RUM-driven steering: real-user beacons feed mapping service choosing best PoP per client-prefix continuously — beats static geo tables (Netflix/OpenConnect-style measurement-driven placement).
• Multi-region active-active prerequisites: data replication strategy (consensus across regions = latency; async = conflict handling), session affinity regional, config propagation.
• Failover drills: region evacuation runbooks rehearsed quarterly; DNS TTL lowering dance pre-event; state reconciliation after split-brain windows.
Interview Answer Template

• Always specify: layer (L4/L7), algorithm + WHY given workload variance, stickiness requirements (usually none if stateless!), health-check strategy, TLS stance.
• Connect to adjacent topics unprompted: consistent-hashing ties to cache farms; outlier-ejection ties to retries/circuit breakers; anycast ties to CDN section — weaving signals mastery.
• Numbers garnish: nginx single node tens-of-thousands rps L7, L4 millions pps; keep-alive reuse multiplying effective capacity.
• Failure-mode storytelling ready: 'backend flaps cause retry storms' → jittered retries + breaker + ejection interplay narrated.
• Anti-pattern callouts: sticky-session crutch for stateful apps (fix statelessness instead), single LB SPOF without VIP/failover pair, health check hitting expensive endpoints.
resources: Power of two random choices survey

hld-caching-cdn.title: Caching & CDNs
hld-caching-cdn.intro: Cache strategy as system design: layering, invalidation, stampedes, eviction science, and edge delivery economics.
groups: Layered Cache Architecture

• Full cake: browser/service-worker → CDN edge → regional shield → app-local LRU (µs, per-pod) → shared Redis/memcached (sub-ms) → DB. Each layer answers 'what's worth keeping closer?'.
• Local+shared combo pattern: tiny local mirror for ultra-hot keys (config flags, feature gates) + shared cluster for long tail; coherence via pub-sub invalidation bus or short local TTLs.
• Hit-ratio compound math: 80% browser × 90% edge × 95% redis → origin sees 0.34% of requests — quote compounding when justifying layers.
• Per-layer TTL doctrine: shorter nearer origin, longer at edge for statics; SWR/stale-if-error resilience headers tie into CN knowledge.
• What NOT to cache: personalized/auth-bound payloads at shared layers (cache-poisoning risk), rapidly-changing inventory without versioned keys.
Invalidation & Coherence Strategy

• TTL-only simplicity: acceptable when staleness budget generous (public pages minutes) — cheapest correct-enough approach; say this before building event machinery!
• Event-driven invalidation: domain events → invalidation stream → precise key purge (tag/surrogate-key APIs at CDNs; prefix-flush patterns in Redis).
• Versioned namespaces escape hatch: bump prefix (v42:user:{id}) on schema/logic change → old entries orphan-expire — atomic mass-invalidation without flush storms.
• Write-through vs invalidate-on-write: updating cache inline risks concurrent-write races (last-writer-stale); invalidation forces next-read refresh — usually safer default.
• Read-your-writes UX: after POST, pin subsequent reads to origin briefly OR update cache synchronously for THAT user's keys — session-scoped coherence tricks.
Stampede Defense Arsenal

• Thundering herd anatomy: hot key expires → N concurrent misses → N origin queries → origin meltdown. Defenses layered:
• Request coalescing/singleflight: process-local loader dedupe (Go singleflight idiom) then cluster-level lock (Redis SETNX lease w/ fencing token) letting ONE worker refresh while others wait briefly.
• Probabilistic early expiration (XFetch): each reader refreshes early with probability ∝ time-since-refresh — mathematically tames herds without locks (cite the XFetch paper).
• Never-expire + background refresher for small hot sets; logical expiry timestamp inside value checked by readers.
• Cold-start warming: deploy hooks/synthetic crawls preheat caches before traffic shifts; marketing-event runbooks include cache-prewarm steps explicitly.
Eviction Science

• LRU intuition fails under scans (one full-table sweep evicts hotset) → LRU-K/segmented LRU (SLRU) fix recency-frequency balance; Redis approximates via sampling-LRU (evict from random sample pool).
• LFU variants: W-TinyLFU (Caffeine) uses count-min-sketch frequency + windowing — state-of-art admission policy; name-drop for cache-library sophistication.
• Admission control beats eviction sometimes: reject cold fills when hit-rate predicted low (bloom-gated admission in some CDNs).
• Memory accounting realities: Redis fragmentation overhead, serializer overhead per entry (~50-100B baseline) — sizing math includes metadata not just payload.
• Workload-aware tuning: scan-heavy analytics clusters use FIFO-ish policies deliberately; latency-critical stores protect top-K via pinned segments.
CDN Deep Mechanics

• Pull vs push, shield-tier origin-protection, miss-latency engineering (persistent origin connections, prefetch-on-hit-adjacent — CDN prefetching popular neighbors).
• Dynamic-content acceleration: route optimization (private backbone vs public internet BGP), TLS/TCP termination near-user with warmed tunnels to origin (Cloudflare Argo-class products).
• Edge compute tier: workers rewriting auth/A-B/personalization at edge; KV stores replicated read-local — blurring CDN↔app boundary trend.
• Cache-key craft: normalize query params, strip tracking junk, vary only on true content-affecting headers; device-class buckets instead of raw UA strings.
• Economics: egress $ dominates; CDN offload percentages reported to finance; multi-CDN steering by RUM telemetry + contract curves — enterprise-grade closing point.
Scenario Drills

• 'Design trending products page': 5s edge TTL + tag-invalidation on inventory events + personalization widget uncached iframe/API — hybrid answer.
• 'Flash sale 100x spike': prewarm entire catalog pre-event, static-render price snapshots, queue waiting room at edge (ticketing pattern), stampede defenses armed.
• 'User complains seeing stale avatar after upload' — cache-key versioned by content-hash/avatar-version counter; purge old key async; read-your-writes pinning immediate post-upload.
• 'Redis cluster at 80% memory' — audit big keys (SCAN --bigkeys), enable LFU if skewed, shard further, compress values (protobuf+zstd), consider local-tier offload.
• 'Origin DB melting despite cache' — measure actual origin QPS composition: likely un-cacheable auth'd endpoints → micro-caching per-user short-TTL, or query-shaping fixes, or read-replica routing.

hld-datastores-scale.title: Datastores at Scale
hld-datastores-scale.intro: Choosing and shaping storage under load: SQL vs NoSQL decisions, sharding refresher, denormalization, polyglot persistence.
groups: Selection Decision Tree

• Interrogate: shape (relational/doc/KV/wide-column/graph/vector/time-series), consistency need (money→strong; feeds→eventual), access patterns (point/range/aggregations), scale horizon, team fluency, ops appetite.
• Default posture: managed Postgres/MySQL until concrete trigger fires — boring-tech-wins narrative with THRESHOLDS named ('reads saturate replicas at X', 'working set exceeds Y').
• Specialized triggers: search → ES/OpenSearch projection; time-series metrics → TSDB (Timescale/Influx/M3); vectors → pgvector start; massive simple-KV → DynamoDB/Cassandra class.
• Escape hatches BEFORE migrations: replicas, caching, archiving tiers, partitioning often defer engine swaps years — enumerate them first in interviews.
• Migration reversibility: avoid hard-to-exit models; export paths tested; dual-write windows planned — reversibility as selection criterion signals wisdom.
Sharding Execution Refresher

• Key choice by access-pattern: user_id for social (all queries user-scoped), tenant_id B2B, geo for locality-sensitive; avoid monotonic timestamps alone (hot tail shard).
• Compound schemes: hash(user)%logical_shards → mapped onto physical (Instagram doctrine); ranges within hash for time-order needs.
• Cross-shard penalties: scatter-gather latency=slowest shard; transactions spanning shards need 2PC/sagas — design access patterns single-shard-first.
• Rebalancing choreography: dual-write → backfill → checksum verify → shadow-read → cutover per unit; throttled movers respect prod IO budgets.
• Global secondary indexes: maintained via change-propagation (DynamoGSIs native; Cassandra/DynamoDB GSI semantics compared) — know their eventual-consistency quirks.
Denormalization Discipline

• Precompute read shapes: counters (likes_count), join-projection tables (feed_items), materialized aggregates refreshed incrementally.
• Sync mechanisms ranked: transactional outbox + async projector (safe default), triggers (DB-coupled but reliable), scheduled reconciliation sweeps catching drift (always include!), CDC pipelines (Debezium) at scale.
• Drift detection: periodic checksum comparisons source-vs-projection; alert on divergence budgets; auto-heal jobs rebuild partitions.
• Consistency labeling per field: which numbers may lag seconds vs must-be-exact — document in data dictionary; product conversations anchored here prevent bugs.
• Write-amplification watch: every denormalized copy taxes every write; measure before stacking fifth copy — consolidation opportunities revisited quarterly.
Polyglot Persistence In Practice

• Canonical stack: relational core + Redis cache + search projection + object storage blobs + warehouse analytics — integration via CDC spine (Debezium→Kafka→consumers).
• Ownership boundaries: one team owns truth-source per entity; projections owned downstream teams with contracts (schema registry discipline).
• Operational surface grows: each store brings backup/upgrade/security matrices — consolidate ruthlessly unless clear win; 'every datastore you run is a pet' quip lands.
• Cross-store consistency stories: saga compensation when money touches multiple stores; idempotent projectors dedupe replays.
• Case anchors: Uber Schemaless (MySQL shards + indexes on HBase-like layer), Discord Cassandra→ScyllaDB evolution, Shopify MySQL sharding at scale — one-liner citations each.
Time-Series & Analytics Stores

• TSDB patterns: time-partitioned hypertables, downsampling rollups (raw 7d → 1m 90d → 1h forever), retention policies automated; tags-vs-fields cardinality discipline (Influx lesson).
• Columnar warehouses: Parquet+object storage decoupled compute (Snowflake/BigQuery/ClickHouse); column pruning + vectorized scans make OLAP cheap.
• Lambda→Kappa evolution: batch+speed layers unified into replayable streams (Flink/Kafka) where feasible — architectural simplification narrative.
• ClickHouse specifics if probed: MergeTree engines, primary-key sparsity, materialized views chaining — hot tech worth one card of depth.
• Lakehouse buzz decoded: Delta/Iceberg/Hudi ACID tables over object storage — schema-evolution + time-travel selling points translated plainly.
Storage Scenario Bank

• 'Design metrics platform': ingestion Kafka → TSDB sharded by day, downsamplers, Grafana serving, retention lifecycle, cardinality guardrails.
• 'Product catalog with faceted search': Postgres truth + ES projection (facets/aggregations) + CDN-cached category pages + admin reindex tooling.
• 'Multi-tenant B2B SaaS isolation spectrum': shared-schema tenant_id → schema-per-tenant → DB-per-tenant cost curve; noisy-neighbor cgroup-style quotas at app layer.
• 'Audit logs immutable 7yr': append-only table + WORM object-storage export, legal-hold flags, partition-drop lifecycle after export verified.
• 'Geo-distributed profiles': home-region authoritative + global cache + conflict-policy per-field (display-name LWW ok, email never) — region-pinning narrative.

hld-consistency-consensus.title: Consistency & Consensus
hld-consistency-consensus.intro: The theory round made practical: consistency models, Raft mechanics, quorum arithmetic, sagas and exactly-once illusions.
groups: Consistency Model Ladder Applied

• Linearizability: operations appear instantaneous globally — needed for locks/leader-election/id-generation; priced in consensus RTTs.
• Sequential/causal middle ground: per-client ordering preserved, causal chains visible (comment-after-post never inverted) — sufficient for most social features.
• Eventual + session guarantees: read-your-writes, monotonic-reads implemented via session tokens/sticky routing — what 'eventually consistent' products actually ship.
• PACELC framing: Partition → AP availability vs CP consistency forced choice; Else → Latency vs Consistency permanent tension — use acronym correctly and explain BOTH halves.
• Feature-to-model mapping drill: cart quantity strong, recommendations eventual, profile causal, payments linearizable — articulate budgets per feature.
Raft Mechanics Walkthrough

• Roles: leader elected by majority term-votes; heartbeat AppendEntries; election timeout randomized 150-300ms preventing split votes.
• Log replication: leader appends → fans out → commits on majority ack → applies to FSM; followers truncate conflicting suffixes on catch-up (safety invariant: only committed entries survive elections).
• Membership changes: joint-consensus or single-server-add steps; snapshotting + log compaction bound growth; InstallSnapshot for far-lagged followers.
• Lease-reads optimization: leader serves reads within lease window sans quorum round-trip — clock-assumed-bounded caveat stated honestly; ReadIndex as safer middle option.
• Production deployments: etcd (k8s meta), Consul, TiKV/Raft-ranges-per-shard storages — cite where YOU'D run it vs embed it.
Quorum Systems Arithmetic

• N=3,R=2,W=2 intersection guarantees overlap; sloppy quorums + hinted handoff trade consistency for availability during churn (Dynamo lineage).
• Conflict resolution menu: last-write-wins (clock trust gamble), vector clocks (causal precision, metadata bloat), CRDT merge functions (bounded convergence), application merge UIs.
• Read-repair/anti-entropy: Merkle-tree range comparison syncing divergent replicas efficiently (Dynamo/Cassandra heritage detail worth naming).
• Tail effects: quorum read latency = max(R samples); straggler probability compounds — tail-tolerant designs hedge reads or accept bounded staleness.
• When quorums suffice vs consensus: tunable-eventual stores for user-tolerant data; consensus for coordination primitives — decision sentence ready.
Distributed Transactions Reality

• 2PC blocking problem: coordinator death strands prepared txns → availability tax; XA horror stories as cautionary lore.
• Sagas: local-txn chains + compensations; choreography (events) vs orchestration (Temporal/Cadence workflows); compensations MUST be idempotent + retryable + handle partial-failure reentry.
• Outbox pattern kills dual-write: state-change + event in SAME local txn; relay publishes via CDC (Debezium) — the standard modern answer, draw the diagram.
• Exactly-once illusions: dedupe keys consumer-side + idempotent producers + transactional offsets (Kafka EOS) make it LOOK once; say the illusion sentence verbatim.
• Calvin/spanner alternatives: deterministic pre-ordering or TrueTime commit-wait buying serializable globally — exotic hardware/tradeoff garnish.
Clocks, Time & Ordering Hazards

• Wall clocks lie: NTP slews/steps, VM pauses past leases, leap smears — never build correctness on cross-node wall-clock comparisons alone.
• Logical clocks: Lamport establishes happens-before partial order; vector clocks capture causality fully (Dynamo context objects); hybrid clock (HLC) bridges both (CockroachDB choice).
• Fencing tokens: monotonic storage-issued tickets invalidating zombie writers post-pause (Kleppmann locking essay — REQUIRED citation for lock discussions).
• Spanner TrueTime: GPS+atomic clocks bounding uncertainty; commit-wait waits out the uncertainty window — external consistency via hardware honesty.
• Practical rules: timeouts ≠ failures (ambiguous outcome! resolve via idempotency/reconciliation), never compare timestamps across nodes for causality claims.
Theory-to-Anecdote Bridges

• Jepsen literacy: cite 2 findings casually (Mongo stale-reads era fixed by majority-default; Elasticsearch pause-resume divergence) — signals you follow anomaly literature.
• CAP incident retellings: Cassandra tunable-consistency misconfigs causing lost updates; Redis-as-lock debates (Redlock controversy both sides summarized).
• TLA+ mainstreaming: AWS/Azure published formal-spec war stories — mention spec-before-code culture for protocol work as aspiration.
• Drill: 'design distributed lock' → lease+token+fencing+clock-skew-bounds+renewal semantics + honest caveats — complete answer template.
• Drill: 'exactly-once order processing' → idempotency keys + outbox + dedupe store + reconciliation sweeper + audit trail — assembled from above pieces fluently.

hld-queues-streaming.title: Queues & Stream Processing
hld-queues-streaming.intro: Async backbones: Kafka internals, delivery semantics, partitioning strategy, stream processing, backpressure.
groups: Why Queues Change System Shape

• Decouple spikes: producers burst freely; consumers drain at sustainable rate — peak-shaving transforms capacity planning (size for average + backlog bounds, not instant peak).
• Failure isolation: downstream brownouts buffer upstream; retries with DLQs quarantine poison messages without blocking lanes.
• Temporal decoupling enables replay: durable logs let consumers reprocess history (bug-fix backfills!) — THE paradigm shift vs RPC thinking.
• Fan-out multiplication: one publish, N independent consumer groups (analytics + notifications + search indexing) — pub/sub semantics with durability.
• Costs named honestly: operational surface, latency floor added, ordering complexities, eventual-consistency debugging skills required.
Kafka Internals Mastery

• Log-structured: append-only partitions, sequential IO, zero-copy sendfile transfers — why it's fast (cite Kafka design doc numbers: high disk-queue-depth irrelevance, 1M+ msg/s commodity nodes).
• Partitions = parallelism + ordering units: keys hash → partition; per-key strict order guaranteed, global order requires single partition (throughput ceiling!).
• Producers: acks=all + min.insync.replicas=2 durability triangle with replication.factor=3; idempotent producer (PID+seq) eliminating broker-side dupes on retry.
• Consumers: pull model with offset commits; consumer groups rebalance via coordinator; static membership avoiding rebalance storms on restart; cooperative-sticky incremental rebalances (stop-the-world killer fixed).
• Retention: time/size-based deletion, log compaction for keyed latest-state topics (changelog semantics), tiered storage to S3 (modern default).
Delivery Semantics Engineering

• At-most-once: fire-and-forget/commit-before-process — losses on crash. At-least-once: retry-until-ack + idempotent consumers (dedupe store keyed message-id) — industry default posture.
• Effectively-once pipeline: idempotent producer + transactional consumer-offset-commit binding (consume-transform-produce atomically) — Kafka EOS mechanics summarized correctly.
• Idempotency implementation menu: dedupe table (processed_ids with TTL), conditional writes (CAS on state machine), natural idempotency (SET operations, upserts).
• Poison-pill handling: retry budget → DLQ with original envelope + error context; DLQ dashboards + replay tooling FIRST-CLASS (unmonitored DLQ = silent data loss).
• Ordering-vs-parallelism tension resolved: order within key only; design keys accordingly (order_id for payment events) — state the guarantee you're relying on.
Consumer Design Patterns

• Batch micro-processing: poll batches, bulk DB writes, commit AFTER success — throughput multiplier + crash-safe (offsets uncommitted until done).
• Long-processing care: max.poll.interval tuning, pause/resume APIs for backpressure, heartbeats decoupled from processing (modern clients).
• Fan-out topologies: topic-per-domain + group-per-consumer; join-streams via KTables/windowed joins in ksql/Flink for enrichment.
• Deadlock-avoidance in multi-topic consumption: consistent acquisition ordering, timeout+retry loops, or single-thread-per-partition confinement.
• Lag as SLO: consumer-lag dashboards + alerts (burstable thresholds), autoscaling consumers bounded by partition count (scaling ceiling named!).
Stream Processing Frameworks

• Kafka Streams: library-in-JVM, exactly-once v2, state stores backed by changelog topics — lightweight default for JVM shops.
• Flink: true streaming (event-time, watermarks, checkpointed state to durable storage), SQL API adoption exploding — the heavyweight answer for complex event-time logic.
• Event-time vs processing-time: watermarks bound lateness; allowed-lateness windows update retroactively — explain watermark concept in ONE clean sentence when asked.
• State management: RocksDB-backed keyed state, checkpoint barriers aligning offsets+state snapshots — recovery = restore + rewind offsets.
• Alternatives context: Spark Structured Streaming micro-batch heritage, Pulsar Functions, cloud-native (Kinesis Analytics) — breadth mention sufficient.
Backpressure & Failure Drills

• End-to-end backpressure chain: bounded queues at every hop, consumers signal via fetch-max-bytes/pause, producers throttle on broker quotas — no component OOMs silently.
· Broker-side quotas: produce/fetch byte-rate limits per client-id protecting cluster fairness (multi-tenant clusters mandatory feature).
• Failure drill narratives: broker loss (ISR shrink → under-min-ISR writes stall — durability held), consumer-group storm during deploy (static membership + cooperative rebalances), poison-message lane isolation verified via chaos test.
• Capacity math: bytes/day ÷ partitions × replication factor → disk; peak MB/s ÷ per-consumer throughput → consumer count; headroom 2x.
• Alternatives fair-compare: SQS managed-simple (visibility timeouts, FIFO queues limits), RabbitMQ routing-rich (exchanges/bindings), NATS jetstream light-fast — pick-by-context fluency.

hld-microservices-patterns.title: Microservices & Integration Patterns
hld-microservices-patterns.intro: When/how to split services, gateway and mesh plumbing, data-decomposition patterns, and the migration playbook from monoliths.
groups: To Split Or Not To Split

• Honest defaults: modular monolith first — module boundaries enforced internally, extract ONLY when scaling/team-topology demands prove it (Amazon/Netflix contexts differ from yours — say so).
• Split drivers ranked: independent deploy cadence per team, differing scaling axes (search CPU vs checkout IO), fault isolation, tech heterogeneity NEEDS.
• Service granularity smell tests: does service own its DATA (not shared DB!)? Can team deploy Friday? Two-pizza team fit? If answers no — premature split.
• Distributed-monolith warning signs: synchronous chains A→B→C→D per request, shared release trains, cross-service DB joins — worse than monolith; name the disease when evaluating designs.
• Team-topology framing: Conway's law leveraged deliberately — service boundaries mirror communication paths; cite 'Team Topologies' vocabulary lightly.
API Gateway & BFF Pattern

• Gateway responsibilities: routing, TLS, authN verification (JWT validation), rate limiting, response shaping, canary routing, observability injection — centralized cross-cutting layer.
• Backend-for-Frontend variant: per-client-type aggregators (mobile-BFF coalesces calls, web-BFF different shape) killing chatty-latency and over-fetching at the edge.
• Pitfalls named: gateway becoming business-logic dump (keep it thin!), single point requiring careful HA, aggregation latency floors — mitigations listed.
• GraphQL federation as alternative aggregation: subgraphs own schemas, gateway composes — when flexibility beats REST simplicity (client-driven shapes) with N+1 resolver cautions.
• Product landscape: Kong/Envoy-Gateway/APISIX self-hosted vs cloud-managed (APIGW/Cloudflare) — selection by ops appetite.
Service Mesh & East-West Plumbing

• Mesh value prop: mTLS everywhere, retries/timeouts/outlier-ejection as SIDEcar policy (app code freed), traffic shifting (canary %), rich L7 telemetry — uniformity across heterogeneous languages.
• Costs equally stated: sidecar resource tax (per-pod proxies), complexity class upgrade, debug-layer indirection — adopt when microservice count × language diversity pays for it (istio/linkerd ambient-mode trends reducing tax).

Data Decomposition Patterns

• Database-per-service rule: shared DB = hidden coupling, schema-change negotiations, blast-radius coupling — the FIRST thing evaluators check in microservice designs.
• Saga family: choreography (events trigger reactions — simple, flow-hidden) vs orchestration (central state-machine workflow — visible, testable; Temporal-style) — pick by flow complexity, justify.
• Outbox + CDC spine: local txn writes domain-state + outbox row; Debezium streams to Kafka; projectors build read-models — THE canonical cross-service consistency answer (draw it unprompted).
• Query-side composition: API-compose (gateway aggregates) vs CQRS read-models (pre-joined views per use-case) — latency/complexity tradeoff articulated.
• Shared-reference-data problem: replicated config/reference tables via versioned broadcasts vs lookup-service calls — staleness budgets per dataset.
Resilience Choreography Between Services

• Timeout budget cascade: total-request budget divided across hops (e.g., 500ms → gateway 50 + svc-A 200 + svc-B 150 + slack) — budgets documented, monitored per-hop.
• Retry policy matrix: WHICH errors (5xx/timeouts yes, 4xx no), how many (2-3), backoff+jitter, retry-budget caps (% of calls), idempotency prerequisite — blind retries amplify outages (retry storm case study reference).
• Circuit breakers per-dependency: open/half-open/closed transitions, fallback behaviors (cached/default/degrade-feature) — breaker dashboards as ops artifacts.
• Bulkheads: per-dependency connection/thread pools isolating slow dependencies from starving unrelated ones — pool-sizing math mentioned.
• Hedged requests: duplicate slow-percentile requests racing (tail-latency killer for idempotent reads — Dean & Barroso tail-tolerance paper cited).
Migration Playbook From Monolith

• Strangler-fig sequence: route-by-endpoint at gateway → new service owns slice behind stable facade → data extracted LAST (sync via CDC until cutover) → retire module.
• Branch-by-abstraction inside monolith pre-split: interfaces at module boundaries make future seams real — internal prep step often skipped, impresses seniors.
• Data extraction choreography: logical separation (schema ownership) → physical move with dual-write/shadow-read verification → cutover flag → cleanup sprint.
• Anti-corruption layers wrapping legacy semantics during transition — DDD vocabulary deployed correctly.
• Success metric honesty: deployment frequency, MTTR, change-failure-rate improvements MEASURED post-split (DORA framing) else revert — outcome-over-fashion stance.
